title: The last gray digest
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. The third gray digest, the last before the machine comes back. The cover: the laundromat's window with the two skeletons still up, one paper, one ink, and now a wreath. The owner has kept the ink one.

panels.composition: The cover: the laundromat window from the street, two skeletons and a wreath, gray.

image.prompt: close on a gray photocopied booklet cover showing a shop window with two skeletons and a wreath, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The real window: the paper skeleton, the ink skeleton, a wreath between them. WOOD outside looking at it. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a laundromat window with a paper skeleton and an ink drawing of a skeleton with a wreath between them, a young man and a dog outside, black and white, no words
a laundromat owner at her counter speaking to a young man in the doorway, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The rack: three gray digests, then the black one from November. The machine comes back in January. The gray ones stay in the rack; nobody takes them. Wood finds that right.

image.prompt: a wire rack holding three faded gray booklets beside one crisp black-and-white one in a laundromat, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'It keeps.' Nobody takes the gray ones. He finds that right.
